question: In the animal kingdom, which of the following phyla includes animals with a segmented body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Annelida**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Annelida is a phylum of segmented worms, which includes earthworms, leeches, and marine worms.
 
• Members of the Annelida phylum have bodies divided into repetitive segments called metameres.
 
• This segmentation allows for greater flexibility and mobility, facilitating burrowing and other locomotive behaviors.
 
• Annelids possess a true coelom, a body cavity completely lined with mesoderm, which aids in the function of their hydrostatic skeleton.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metamerism:** This refers to the segmentation of the body into a series of repeated units, which is a key characteristic of Annelida.
 
• **Closed Circulatory System:** Annelids have a closed circulatory system, meaning that blood is enclosed within blood vessels and is pumped by a heart.
 
• **Setae:** Many annelids possess small bristle-like structures called setae on each segment, which help in locomotion and anchorage.
 
• **Ecological Role:** Annelids play a significant role in soil health as decomposers and by aerating the soil, which is vital for plant growth.
 
• **Clitellum:** In earthworms, a thickened, glandular section of the body known as the clitellum secretes mucus during reproduction, aiding in the transfer of sperm and the formation of a cocoon for the developing embryos.
